messages:
jun.park: quick idea — run a tiny sanity probe on "speculative acceptance with sample-weighting" (not the usual topk-spec). goal: reduce wasted speculative decodes by biasing acceptance toward higher-weight samples, see latency delta + quality regression risk.

maria.g: short version: add a per-sample weight w_i in the acceptance rule. acceptance if p_candidate / p_spec >= tau * w_i. weights from calibrated softprompt score or eval metric.

eli: can you sketch exact rule? hard to follow in head. also which models/quant levels?

jun.park: sure. rule: accept if (p_candidate / p_speculative) >= tau * (1 + alpha*(w_i - 0.5)). where w_i in [0,1], alpha in [0,0.4]. tau baseline 0.8. proto snippet:```python
def accept(p_c, p_s, w, tau=0.8, alpha=0.2):
    return (p_c / p_s) >= tau * (1 + alpha*(w-0.5))
```
run on llama3-12b-4bit and llama3-70b-4bit quant with our usual eval set (convQA + summarization subset).

sam.k: nice. how compute w_i cheaply? full rerank is expensive.

maria.g: use the prefix quality predictor we already have: 128-token chunk, cheap MLP on pooled embeddings => scalar in [0,1]. we already compute that for rerank experiments so reuse.

eli: timeline? we can microbench on a single p3-dedicated shard for latency numbers. I'll spare a 1hr window.

jun.park: planned runs: (1) baseline topk-spec (tau=0.8) (2) weighted-accept alpha=0.2 (3) weighted-accept alpha=0.4 (4) conservative tau=0.9 + alpha=0.2. measure median latency, p50/p95, token throughput, and ROUGE/QA EM.

ops-bot: deploy noted: test-shard p3d-1 reserved 30m window starting 1979992000. :rocket:

sam.k: any expected quality regressions? my intuition: slight score variance on abstractive summarization when alpha high, could raise hallucination. recommend turning on sample-weight floor 0.2 to avoid extreme rejection.

jun.park: good call. we'll clamp w_i to [0.2,0.95]. also log cases where acceptance flips decisions so we can hit replay eval.

maria.g: tiny ask — add eval buckets: short (<64 tokens) vs long (>256) and by prefix predictor quartile. we saw acceptance behavior vary by length last time.

eli: noted. also capture kv-cache hit rates and wasted speculative compute (speculative tokens decoded but later dropped).

jun.park: quick early numbers from a 200-sample pilot on 12b-4bit (alpha=0.2): median latency -8%, p95 -3%, ROUGE-L delta -0.6 pts, EM unchanged. wasted spec tokens down 12%. looks promising but small N.

sam.k: -0.6 ROUGE is in-line with what we'd expect for this perf gain, still want larger eval. can we run 2k samples next?

maria.g: add automated quality alarms: if any metric drops >1.2 points OR hallucination rate > baseline+0.5% then flag rollback.

jun.park: agreed. plan: 2k run tomorrow on 70b-4bit dedicated shard, then decide canary. if results similar, propose a canary rollout to 5% traffic with trace-level logging for 24h.

eli: thumbs up from infra side. please post the experiment ID and seed.

jun.park: exp id spec-wt-1979991234, seeds [42,99]. I'll push logs to /experiments/spec-wt/1979991234 and include diff repro snippets.

maria.g: thanks — one more: include prompt calibration set (we saw mismatch earlier). otherwise lgtm.

jun.park: will do. tagging @sam.k to review rollout policy doc before canary. :eyes:

sam.k: will take a look after lunch.

ops-bot: experiment spec-wt-1979991234 created and linked to shard test-shard. artifacts: s3://redwood-exps/spec-wt/1979991234.

eli: perfect. catching up later after 2k run.
